identity.description: Unpenalized maximum-likelihood softmax classifier over K unordered categories, fit by Newton's method: (K-1) coefficient equations against a reference category, each with standard errors, z-tests, and confidence intervals. The multiclass inference sibling of ols — choose it to EXPLAIN category choice; choose sklearn's logistic_regression to predict it.

consumes.note: target must be integer-coded 0..K-1; code 0 becomes the reference category all coefficients are relative to

emits.note: argmax over the probability matrix — wrapper-derived, not a separate library call
a (p+1)x(K-1) matrix of log-odds-vs-reference effects with bse/pvalues/conf_int — the genuine multiclass inference emission

method.note: fit() optimizer; newton uses the exact Hessian (also the SE source), bfgs/lbfgs for large p

maxiter.note: the statsmodels default of 35 is famously low — raise it before diagnosing anything else on non-convergence

hyperparameters.note: no regularization knob in plain fit() — nothing searchable; fit_regularized(alpha=...) exists as the L1 escape hatch for separation but forfeits the clean SE story

invariances.why: coefficients are per-unit log-odds against the reference category, and Newton's step inverts a Hessian whose conditioning degrades with unscaled features — ill-scaling is a real convergence failure mode, not just cosmetics
log-odds are assumed linear in the supplied columns; a monotone transform is a different specification
the likelihood has no missingness model; NaN raises (or missing='drop' listwise-deletes with the usual bias)
the array API needs a pre-encoded design matrix; the target additionally needs integer coding
assumes IIA (independence of irrelevant alternatives): the odds between any two categories are unaffected by the others — the red-bus/blue-bus failure; plus linear log-odds per equation
fits (K-1)*(p+1) parameters and the effective sample is the SMALLEST category — K inflates the parameter count and rare classes starve their equations
each linear log-odds equation extends beyond the training range; probabilities saturate but rankings keep shifting

featureStats.why: with (K-1)*(p+1) parameters, the binding sample size is the smallest category — a rare class drives quasi-separation and exploding SEs in its equation
collinearity inflates SEs simultaneously across ALL K-1 equations, multiplying the interpretability damage relative to the binary case
any feature perfectly predicting one category sends its unpenalized MLE coefficient to infinity (Hauck-Donner effect) — plain fit() has no penalty to stop it

modelMetrics.why: 1 - llf/llnull is the likelihood-native fit share — the honest scoreboard where R2 has no meaning for a discrete MLE
the SEs ARE the inverse Hessian's diagonal — near-singularity from collinearity or separation makes the entire inference table garbage even if predictions look fine

edgeCases.behavior: coefficient diverges, Hessian goes singular, SEs explode (Hauck-Donner)
edgeCases.note: fit_regularized(alpha) or the penalized sklearn sibling — at the cost of the SE story

edgeCases.behavior: that equation's coefficients are estimated from a handful of rows — huge SEs, fragile fit
(K-1)*(p+1) parameter blow-up; slow Newton steps and overfit risk
biased substitution patterns — the red-bus/blue-bus pathology
edgeCases.note: nested/mixed logit is the econometric fix, outside this catalog

edgeCases.behavior: ConvergenceWarning; params from an unfinished Newton run
edgeCases.note: raise maxiter and scale features before any other diagnosis

driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: add_constant on the design matrix; label-encode target to 0..K-1 and remember the mapping (0 = reference); predict() returns the K-column probability matrix — argmax + decode for class-label; expose params/bse/pvalues/conf_int per equation as the coefficients payload
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded Newton fit; predict on the results object is thread-safe

placementClaims.why: no missingness model — NaN raises or is listwise-deleted, biasing the choice shares
linearizing skewed covariates improves the linear-log-odds specification each equation assumes
Newton's Hessian inversion is the SE source AND the optimizer — ill-conditioned unscaled features cause real convergence failures and incomparable per-unit coefficients
features must be design-encoded (reference level dropped to avoid the dummy trap) and the target integer-coded
